ac-b2f.description: QFX5110-32Q-AFI: two 650 W AC supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5110-32Q-FANAFI). All have a Juniper Azure Blue handle and the label AIR IN or AFI (guide Tables 11 and 13).

ac-f2b.description: QFX5110-32Q-AFO: two 650 W AC supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5110-32Q-FANAFO). All have a Juniper Gold handle and the label AIR OUT or AFO (guide Tables 11 and 13).

chas.description: QFX5110-32Q-CHAS, the spare chassis, shipped without power supplies or fan modules (guide Table 3: "Order PSUs separately. Fan modules are not shipped by default."). AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fan modules are ordered separately. Supplies and fans of one airflow only go in. The supply and fan bays are shown open.

dc-b2f.description: QFX5110-32Q-DC-AFI: two 650 W DC supplies (JPSU-650W-DC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5110-32Q-FANAFI). The front panel is the same.

dc-f2b.description: QFX5110-32Q-DC-AFO: two 650 W DC supplies (JPSU-650W-DC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5110-32Q-FANAFO). The front panel is the same.

description: Juniper QFX5110-32Q, a 1RU data-centre spine and leaf switch running Junos OS. It has 28 QSFP+ ports and 4 QSFP28 ports. A QSFP+ port runs at 40 GbE, or as four 10 GbE ports with a breakout cable. A QSFP28 port runs at 100 GbE or 40 GbE. The port side also carries the RJ-45 grandmaster clock port and the 10 MHz and 1 PPS outputs. The rear carries two power supplies, five fan modules, the console, two management ports, a USB port, the reset button and the four chassis lamps. One front panel ships in four power and airflow variants. They have AC or DC supplies, with airflow front-to-back (AIR OUT) or back-to-front (AIR IN). A spare chassis ships without supplies or fan modules.

gaps.wanted: Table 19 gives the rated operating voltage as -39 to -60 VDC and the operating range as -40 through -72 VDC, with the current rated at 8.2 A at 39 VDC. Both are transcribed as printed.

The QFX5110 datasheet (the token is the nearest the schema offers: the document exists but was not readable). Its address redirects to an HPE document viewer (a00150813enw) that did not answer in three tries, so its ordering table, weight and power were not read.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port "for image updates" and gives no generation. It is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The guide's text calls the 10 MHz and 1 PPS connections SubMiniature B (SMB); the photograph shows threaded jacks 7.5 mm across, drawn as the registry's SMA. The photograph is followed, estimated.
The studio photograph shows a green lamp in each upper corner of the GM jack. The guide's tables do not name them, so they are not modelled.

A photograph of the rear. The guide's drawing is the only picture: the fan numbers, the fan and power icons and the model chip are read from it, and the chip text is that of the drawing, not a confirmed print.
The laser-safety triangle at the lower right of the port side and the corner mark at the upper right. They are labels, not features of the metal, and are not drawn.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD terminal on the port side (guide figure 15, callout 1)

fan-leds.description: The status lamp at the left of each fan slot - green when the module works, blinking amber on an error (guide Table 12).

attrs.redundancy-note: QFX5110 hardware guide (2026-09-24), Cooling System and Airflow Description: "All fan modules must be installed for optimal operation of the switch" and the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced. The guide states no N+1 form, so no spare fan is claimed.

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band cluster at the left of the rear - an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, two SFP management ports, a USB port and the recessed reset button. Four kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: two supplies, load-sharing; one may be removed at a time while the switch runs

qsfp-plus.description: Ports 0 to 27, the even ports on the upper row. Each runs at 40 GbE, or as four 10 GbE ports with a breakout cable.

qsfp-plus-channel-leds.description: The second to fourth lamps of each QSFP+ port, in port then lane order - used when the port runs as four 10 GbE ports (guide Table 6).

qsfp-plus-leds.description: The first of the four lamps of each QSFP+ port - used for a 40 GbE link (guide Tables 6 and 8).

qsfp28.description: Ports 28 to 31 as printed, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 28. Each runs at 100 GbE or 40 GbE.

qsfp28-channel-leds.description: The second to fourth lamps of each QSFP28 port, in port then lane order - used when the port runs as four 10 GbE ports (guide Table 6).

qsfp28-leds.description: The first of the four lamps of each QSFP28 port - used for a 100 GbE or unchannelized 40 GbE link (guide Table 6).

status-leds.description: The four chassis lamps ALM, SYS, MST and ID (guide Table 10).

timing.mixed: the grandmaster clock cluster at the left of the port side - an RJ-45 grandmaster clock jack and the 10 MHz and 1 PPS output connectors. Two kinds, one purpose: carrying the time reference to and from the switch.

name: qfx5110-32q

chassis.note: guide Table 24: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.1 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52.02 cm) deep excluding the fan and power supply handles, 24.6 lb (11.16 kg) with two power supplies. 1.72 in is 43.7 mm and 4.3 cm is 43 mm; the inch figure is carried, as the 1RU height. The width is the body: the mounting brackets are not part of it and are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate samples #767b82 (a 15 by 20 px mean on the plate left of the port block, #81868c at the right end) in the studio photograph. The photograph is lit and these are its values, not a paint reference. The rear has no photograph and carries the same chassis colour.

drawing-vs-photo.note: On this model the guide's figure 15 and the photograph agree: 10M OUT is the left jack and PPS OUT the right one (callouts 3 and 4). The guide's text calls the pair "SubMiniature B (SMB)" connectors; the photograph shows threaded SMA-style jacks 7.5 mm across, drawn as the registry's SMA (see gaps). The guide's figure 15 prints "GM" under the RJ-45 jack, as the photograph does.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the rack mount kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (a partial toolless four-post kit: a pair of front and rear mounting rails, a pair of mounting brackets and sixteen M4 x 6 mm screws, orderable as a spare), for rails 23.5 to 30.6 in (59.7 to 77.7 cm) apart front to back (Table 25), flush with the front of the rack or recessed 2 in (5 cm) with the extension bracket. Rack kits are recorded here and not modelled in this slice, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets. Figure 71 shows a supply installed in a 32Q with an EMI gasket; the guide does not otherwise describe the gasket.

front-left.note: Left of the port block, read off the photograph at 3 times and scaled at 4.405 px/mm: the RJ-45 grandmaster jack (GM, callout 2) centred 17.4 mm from the left and 14.4 mm below the top; two gold coaxial jacks 7.5 mm across, 10M OUT centred at 34.7 mm and PPS OUT at 49.5 mm from the left, both 16.7 mm below the top; the ESD symbol at 7.2 mm, 31.6 mm and the ESD jack below it at 7.2 mm, 38.8 mm. The lamps in the corners of the GM jack are green in the photograph; the guide names no function for them, so they are not modelled as lamps (see gaps).

gate-1.note: Front: the studio photograph. Its body is 1942 px wide (columns 91 to 2033) and 192.5 px high (rows 137.0 to 329.5), an aspect of 10.09 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09. Scale 4.405 px/mm both ways. The photograph is turned about 0.15 degrees: the port rows sit about 1.1 mm higher at the right end than at the left. Positions are read at the middle of the face and the bracket round the 100G ports, read at the right end, is carried 0.55 mm down. Rear: figure 16, a raster drawing 1500 px wide whose body outline is 1449 x 146.5 px, an aspect of 9.89, 2 percent out; the positions along the width are taken at 3.286 px/mm and those down the height at 3.35 px/mm. Figure 15 is a 1500 px flat drawing of the front used only to count and to read the printing.

hundred-gig.note: A box is printed round ports 28 to 31: a line above 28 and 30 and below 29 and 31, broken for the numerals, closed at the right end and lettered 100G beside it. It is drawn from the photograph as a printed path and a legend.

lifecycle.note: Searched the guide for an end-of-life notice and found none; the guide is dated 2026-09-24. No announcement for the QFX5110-32Q was looked for at Juniper's end-of-life pages, so the device states none announced, estimated.

mgmt.note: Figure 17 and its key: em0 is the RJ-45 management port C0 (callout 2, lower jack), and the key's callout 2 also names an additional SFP management port, "the second C0" (upper SFP cage); em1 is the SFP management port C1 (callout 5, lower SFP cage); callout 3 is the RJ-45 console port CON (upper jack). The guide says that if both C0 ports are cabled the copper one takes priority. Table 9 gives the lamps. The drawing shows no lamps on the SFP cages.

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX5110-32Q-FANAFO and QFX5110-32Q-FANAFI, juniper/qfx5110-32q-fanafo and qfx5110-32q-fanafi) and the 650 W power supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO, -AFI, -DC-AFO and -DC-AFI, reused from juniper/qfx5100-jpsu-650w-*) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Guide Table 11 (pp. 40-41) names a fan module for each model and airflow, and p. 44 says to use only the one designed for the product number, so the 48S has its own. The guide says to fit a blank panel over an empty power supply slot but names no part number for it, so no blank is modelled. The spare chassis QFX5110-32Q-CHAS ships without supplies or fan modules (Table 3), so its configuration shows every bay open.

port-lamps.note: Four dots stand at 4.1 mm pitch above each upper cage and below each lower one, centred on the cage and 7.6 mm and 37.3 mm below the top edge (Tables 5, 6 and 8, bi-colour). The first lamp of a port is the link lamp of an unchannelized port; the other three are channel lamps (Table 6).

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 15: ports run 0 to 31, even above the upper row and odd below the lower row, the numeral centred over or under each cage between the cage and its four lamps. The guide's text numbers the QSFP+ ports 0 through 27 and the QSFP28 ports 28 through 31. Interface names are not printed on the unit and the guide's front-panel text does not state them, so none is written to the manifest.

ports.note: Front photograph, dividers between cages found as bright columns across the opening: 32 cages in four groups of four columns, each column a pair, on a pitch of 83.7 px, 19.0 mm, which is the registry's qsfp-ganged pitch. The groups start at 394, 798, 1202.5 and 1606.5 px, a stride of 404.2 px, 91.76 mm, so the gutter is 91.76 - 4 x 19.0 = 15.76 mm, and the first cage starts at 68.8 mm from the left edge. Ports 0 to 27 are QSFP+ and 28 to 31 QSFP28 (the guide's callouts 5 and 6 of figure 15); the last group holds QSFP+ ports 24 to 27 and QSFP28 ports 28 to 31 on one pitch. The cells use the registry's 18.5 x 9.58 aperture for both; the photographed cage faces are 8.9 mm high because they include the bezel. QSFP+ and QSFP28 share a cage size and are told apart by their legends and the bracket.

power.note: guide Table 14 (AC): 90 to 264 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 3.6 A at 90 VAC, typical 132 W and maximum 200 W for the 32Q. Table 19 (DC): rated -39 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 through -72 VDC, -8.2 A at 39 VDC, the same 132 W typical and 200 W maximum. The guide's note: maximum measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build; the DC feed is carried under its own keys.

rear-drawing-vs-text.note: Figure 16 draws back-to-front fans (AIR IN) beside supplies lettered AFO. The two cannot be mixed (Tables 11, 13 and 18), so the drawing mixes two builds. The default configuration here is front-to-back with Juniper Gold handles per Tables 13 and 18; the AFI configuration is the blue build. Figure 16 is not followed for the lettering.

rear-layout.note: Figure 16, the flat drawing of the FRU end, with figure 17 for the management panel, both read at 3.5 times; the rear is the same for both models of the family. There is no photograph of the rear: the studio rear photograph returned a 404 page. At the left a 63.2 mm panel carries the QFX5110 and RUNNING JUNOS chip and the logo (not drawn), the four chassis lamps ALM, SYS, MST and ID, two stacked SFP cages (C0 above C1), the console and C0 jacks stacked in one shield, the USB port and the reset pinhole. Then five fan slots on a 48.95 mm pitch, each preceded by a fan icon, its number 0 to 4 and a status lamp, then two supply slots on a 60.8 mm pitch, each preceded by a power icon and its number 0 or 1. The fan and supply slots measure 40.9 x 41.6 mm and 54.8 x 39.8 mm, which are the sizes of the components that seat there. Every position is estimated from a drawing 2 percent out in aspect.

row-pitch.note: Down the columns the cage faces run from row 185 to 224 and 243 to 282 px, centres 15.3 and 28.5 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 13.2 mm. y is good to about 0.5 mm because of the tilt.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5110 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-09-24, 228 pages (Juniper Networks, address below; terms: the guide's copyright notice and the Juniper EULA it names, a reference copy kept outside the repository). Tables 3 (models and part numbers), 5, 6, 8 to 10 (lamps), 11 (fan modules), 13 and 14 (AC supplies), 18 to 20 (DC supplies), 22 (environment), 24 (physical specification); figures 13 and 15 (port panel), 16 to 19 (rear and management panel), 20 to 27 (fan modules, airflow and supplies). Juniper's studio photograph of the 32Q front (image library, qfx5110-32q-front-high, 2100 x 497 px). The datasheet is at a Juniper address that redirects to an HPE document viewer (a00150813enw); it did not answer, so no datasheet figure is used and none is cited. The studio photograph of the rear (qfx5110-32q-rear-high) returned an HTML 404 page, so the rear has only the guide's drawings. No Visio stencil or 3D model was available, and none is named by the guide.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md): the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, so both lips face the band between the rows. The photograph shows the latch lip at the top of the upper cages' openings and the foot of the lower ones; the convention is applied.

vents.note: Two staggered rows of hexagonal holes along the top edge (0.9 to 5.4 mm) and one along the bottom (40.4 to 43.5 mm), the length of the port field, and a patch of hexagons in each of the three gutters between the groups, 9.4 mm wide and 27.6 mm high. They are drawn as vent strips; the hexagon pitch is estimated from the photograph at 3 times, as the pattern is a rectangular approximation of a staggered hexagon field.

placements.description: Table 10 - red: major hardware fault, the switch halted; amber: minor alarm; unlit: no alarm or halted
Table 10 - green steady: Junos OS loaded; green blinking: member of a Virtual Chassis or Virtual Chassis Fabric; unlit: off or halted
Table 10 - green steady: standalone switch or the primary; green blinking: backup primary; unlit: a line card member
Table 10 - blue blinking: the beacon feature is enabled (request chassis beacon); unlit: not enabled
Table 9 - the status lamp is green at 1000 Mbps and amber at 100 Mbps, unlit at 10 Mbps or link down; the link activity lamp is green steady with a link and blinking with traffic

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. No figure shows the right wall flat.
